title: PlayIQ — Sports Analytics Dashboard
description: Built a multi-sport analytics dashboard covering MLB, NBA, WNBA, NFL, NHL and NCAAB, with per-game deep dives across matchup, form, roster and sport-specific modeling tabs. Engineered transparent projection models — Log5 batter-vs-pitcher matchups, Binomial and Poisson distributions, additive scoring — where every output carries a methodology entry naming its source, inputs and formula. Trained an XGBoost model for MLB first-five-innings outcomes offline via a GitHub Actions workflow, and integrated Claude for context-aware game analysis.

insights.summary: A dark-mode sports intelligence dashboard built deliberately without a build step — React 18 and Babel Standalone from a CDN, and a pure Node http/https backend with zero npm dependencies. The design goal was transparency: apart from one XGBoost model, every projection is inspectable arithmetic that explains where its number came from.
highlights: Designed a slate-triage system that badges games (HOT PLAY / LEAN / LOOK / FADE) so the highest-signal matchups surface before drilling in
Built an Edge Finder using Log5 matchup math with per-player threshold projections across MLB, NBA and WNBA
Implemented a live MLB feed with scoreboard, base state, measured pitch locations and play-by-play on a 10-second cache floor
Automated offline model training through a CI workflow so the first-5-innings model retrains without touching the runtime
Kept every non-ML score attached to a `why` string naming its endpoint, inputs and formula

artifacts.alt: PlayIQ dashboard — sport selection with live data indicators

title: Chroma — U-Fund Crowdfunding Platform
description: Built a full-stack charitable crowdfunding platform with a team of four, where donors browse funding Needs, group them into Bundles, manage a shopping cart and maintain recurring Subscriptions. Implemented the Java REST API across layered controller, model and DAO tiers with file-backed persistence, and the Angular front-end covering authentication, dashboard, search, detail views and checkout. Backed the API with a JUnit suite spanning controller, model and persistence layers.

insights.summary: A four-person Agile project structured around a clean separation of concerns: Angular components talk to a Spring REST API, which routes through controllers to a DAO persistence layer, so storage can change without touching business logic. The API ships with a JUnit suite covering all three tiers.
highlights: Designed five domain resources — Needs, Bundles, Shopping Cart, Subscriptions and Users — each with its own controller, model and DAO
Built 15 Angular components covering login/register, dashboard, needs and subscription search, detail views and checkout
Separated DAO interfaces from file-backed implementations so persistence is swappable without changing controllers
Wrote JUnit coverage across controller, model and persistence tiers
Configured CORS and environment-specific API endpoints for local development

title: ACL Unplanned Surgery Predictive Model
description: Accessed UPMC database of de-identified ACLR patients (2013-2021) for predictive modeling. Executed complex SQL queries with CTEs and LEFT JOINs to aggregate clinical datasets. Built logistic regression models using Social Determinants of Health (SDoH) factors to predict unplanned surgery needs.

artifacts.alt: Research poster — Enhancing Prediction of Unplanned Surgeries After ACL Reconstruction: Evaluating the Role of Activity Level Among SDoH Factors

title: Stock Dip Analysis API
description: Built a TypeScript and Express service that scores whether a well-known stock is in a dip worth researching further. Integrated Finnhub for quotes, candles and company news with an Alpha Vantage fallback, and computed RSI locally from candle closes when the upstream indicator endpoint was unavailable. Implemented a capped 100-point rule-based scoring model that weighs dip depth against SMA50, RSI and news sentiment, then labels each result GOOD DIP, WATCH or AVOID.

insights.summary: A deliberately conservative screening API: it flags stocks worth a closer look rather than claiming any is a buy, and it leaves out valuation, full fundamentals and analyst ratings instead of pretending to model them. The scoring rules are fixed and published, so any label can be traced back to the four inputs that produced it.
highlights: Designed a transparent 100-point scoring model: dip depth (30), price above SMA50 (25), RSI below 35 (20), and absence of bad-news keywords (25)
Built an Alpha Vantage fallback path for historical candles when Finnhub restricts the endpoint on free-tier keys
Calculated RSI locally from candle closes rather than depending on a provider indicator endpoint
Added a response cache and normalizer layer to keep third-party rate limits from reaching the scoring path
Containerized the service with Docker Compose alongside a seeded PostgreSQL instance

title: Movie Database Management Systems
description: Built and deployed a PostgreSQL movie database and application using Python and SQL. Collaborated with a group of 5 to design and develop the database and application features. Developed a Python application with SSH tunneling for secure remote database access and management.

insights.summary: A team-of-five database project built around an ETL pipeline: raw Kaggle CSVs are cleaned and normalized, loaded into PostgreSQL under a designed relational schema, then queried through a Python application layer organized into auth, user, movie and collection modules.
highlights: Designed a normalized relational schema supporting search, analytics and queries like top-rated films, genre breakdown and actor co-appearances
Built an ETL pipeline ingesting and cleaning Kaggle CSV datasets before load
Structured the application into auth, user, movie and collection modules over a shared connection layer
Used SSH tunneling for secure remote access to the database server
Documented Docker and manual setup paths so the project runs locally either way

title: Race Condition Detective
description: Diagnosed and repaired race conditions across five intentionally broken concurrent C# components — a bank ledger, counter, cache, logger and queue. Traced each defect to its specific non-atomic read-modify-write sequence and shared mutable state, then selected the narrowest correct fix for each case rather than applying a blanket lock. Documented every bug with its location, the threading interleaving that triggers it, the applied fix, and why that fix restores correctness.

insights.summary: An exercise in reading concurrent code for what it actually compiles to rather than what it looks like. The core insight repeated across the bugs: operations that read as single statements — `_count++`, or assigning a computed balance — are read-modify-write sequences that two threads can interleave, silently losing one update.
highlights: Verified every fix against a randomized harness: 10/10 trials passing on all five components, 15/15 points
Identified lost updates in bank deposit/withdraw from non-atomic read-modify-write on shared balance state
Replaced `_count++` with `Interlocked.Increment` to make the increment a single atomic instruction instead of paying for a full lock
Matched each fix to its failure mode — locks where a critical section spans multiple operations, interlocked primitives where one word is updated
Wrote a structured analysis for every bug covering location, shared state, why it fails, the fix, and why the fix holds

artifacts.alt: Race Condition Detective verification harness — all five components fixed

title: Wildfire Simulation
description: Designed and implemented a C-based wildfire simulation modeling probabilistic fire propagation across a grid-based forest. Developed probabilistic fire spread algorithms incorporating neighbor states, tree density, and burn probability with Fisher–Yates random initialization. Enhanced simulation performance and accuracy through iterative debugging, modular refactoring, and thorough documentation.

artifacts.alt: Wildfire simulation output showing fire spreading across the forest grid

insights.summary: A grid-based cellular simulation where fire spreads probabilistically from burning cells to neighboring trees. Every parameter — grid size, tree density, catch probability, initial burn proportion and the neighbor threshold that influences ignition — is set at the command line, so different fire regimes can be compared directly. Compiles clean under -Wall -Wextra -pedantic.
highlights: Implemented probabilistic spread where ignition depends on the proportion of burning neighbors against a configurable threshold
Built two display modes: an overlay mode that redraws in place and a print mode that emits N discrete time steps
Tracked per-cycle and cumulative state changes to detect when the simulation reaches equilibrium
Used Fisher–Yates shuffling for unbiased random placement of trees across the grid
Separated grid simulation from rendering into distinct modules built via Makefile

title: Pathfinding Search Algorithms
description: Implemented and compared BFS, DFS and A* search over a US state-capital road network loaded from external city and edge datasets. Built an A* heuristic using straight-line distance between coordinates to guide expansion toward the goal, and structured the search layer so each algorithm shares a common graph representation. Benchmarked the three strategies on identical routes to measure path quality against search effort.

insights.summary: A direct comparison of three classical search strategies on the same weighted graph. Running Olympia to Tallahassee makes the trade-off concrete: A* matches BFS on hop count but returns a route 1,055 miles shorter, while DFS wanders to 19 hops and 8,292 miles.
highlights: Measured on Olympia to Tallahassee: A* 8 hops / 4751 mi, BFS 8 hops / 5806 mi, DFS 19 hops / 8292 mi
Implemented A* with a straight-line-distance heuristic over geographic city coordinates
Loaded the road network from separate city and edge data files into a shared graph structure
Designed a common search interface so BFS, DFS and A* run against identical inputs for fair comparison

artifacts.alt: BFS vs A* route comparison from Olympia to Tallahassee

title: Astros and Hoppers
description: Developed Astros and Hoppers, an interactive Java puzzle game with custom mechanics and logic-driven challenges. Partnered to implement a BFS-based shortest-path system that powers core gameplay decisions and guarantees correct pathfinding behavior. Built the JavaFX game board UI and integrated department-provided image assets for a polished player experience, while supporting both GUI and PTUI (text-based) interaction via the command line.

title: Evolutionary Stable Strategy Simulation
description: Built a Hawk-Dove simulation in Python to explore how Evolutionarily Stable Strategies emerge from simple encounter rules. Modeled a configurable population competing over a finite resource where hawk aggression carries a survival cost, driven through an interactive menu that supports stepping through single encounters or running batches of 1,000 to 10,000 interactions. Exposed population size, hawk percentage, resource amount and hawk cost as command-line parameters to make equilibrium conditions directly testable.

insights.summary: A parameter-driven study of the classic Hawk-Dove game. The simulation makes the central result tangible: the stable strategy mix is governed by the ratio of hawk cost to resource value, not by how many hawks start in the population — when cost exceeds the resource, aggression collapses regardless of its initial share.
highlights: Verified the core ESS result at runtime: with resource 50 and hawk cost 100, hawk-hawk encounters kill both participants while dove pairs split +25 each
Modeled hawk-hawk, hawk-dove and dove-dove encounters with distinct payoff and survival outcomes
Demonstrated that hawk cost relative to resource amount drives equilibrium more than initial hawk percentage
Exposed every simulation variable as a command-line argument with sensible defaults for reproducible runs
Separated individual, simulation and entry-point concerns into distinct modules

artifacts.alt: Hawk-Dove simulation output showing hawk-hawk mutual elimination

title: Reaction Timing Racing Game
description: Developed a multiplayer reaction-time racing game for Roblox where players advance along a ten-line track by tapping within a timed window after a randomized flash. Implemented the authoritative server game loop handling countdown, intermission, flash scheduling and win detection, paired with a separate client script for input and feedback. Centralized all tuning — flash windows, cooldowns, track geometry, lane spacing and monetization IDs — into a single shared configuration module.

insights.summary: A server-authoritative multiplayer game built with an external toolchain rather than inside Roblox Studio — Rojo syncs a real filesystem project into the engine, so the code lives in version control like any other repository. Game feel is driven entirely by a single config module, making balance changes a one-line edit.
highlights: Built a server-authoritative loop covering intermission, countdown, randomized flash timing and win detection
Split responsibilities across ServerScriptService, StarterPlayerScripts and a shared ReplicatedStorage module
Randomized flash intervals within a tuned delay range so players cannot pattern-match the timing
Designed gamepass abilities (Reflex Boost extending the tap window, Eliminator with a cooldown) around the core timing mechanic
Used Rojo and Aftman to keep the project in version control instead of inside Roblox Studio
